drug_class: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor (targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Dasatinib is used to treat certain types of leukemia, including chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and a type called Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL). It helps control or slow down the growth of cancer cells. Your doctor prescribes it when other treatments haven't worked well enough or as a first-line treatment.
how_it_works: Your leukemia is driven by an abnormal protein called BCR-ABL, which tells cancer cells to grow out of control. Dasatinib works like a key that blocks this protein, essentially turning off the signal that makes cancer cells multiply. By blocking this signal, the drug slows or stops the growth of leukemia cells.
common_side_effects: Fluid buildup (especially around the lungs, causing shortness of breath), low blood counts (which can cause tiredness, easy bruising, or increased risk of infection), nausea, diarrhea, headache, skin rash, and muscle or joint pain. Feeling tired is also very common.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or swelling — this could mean fluid is building up around your lungs or heart. Dasatinib can lower your blood counts, making you more prone to infections or bleeding. It can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor about all other medications you take. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it can increase drug levels in your body. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn or nursing baby.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is one tablet taken by mouth once a day (100 mg for CML or 140 mg for Ph+ ALL), with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or cut it. Your doctor may adjust your dose depending on how you respond and how well you tolerate the medication. Always take it at the same time each day.
